findings.source_quote: καὶ ἄλλως ἄνθρωπος οὐ δύναται εὑρεθῆναι εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἐὰν μὴ αὗται αὐτὸν ἐνδύσωσι τὸ ἔνδυμα αὐτῶν· ἐὰν γὰρ τὸ ὄνομα μόνον λάβῃς, τὸ δὲ ἔνδυμα παρὰ τούτων μὴ λάβῃς, οὐδὲν ὠφελήσῃ
findings.english_quote: A person cannot otherwise be found in God’s kingdom unless they clothe that person in their garment. For if you receive only the name, but do not receive the garment from them, you will gain nothing.
findings.issue: The rendering follows the selected working Greek, but its editorial status is incompletely disclosed. The supplied apparatus reports ἄλλως as Anger’s conjecture against Athos ἄλλος, and ὠφελήσῃ as Gebhardt’s conjecture against Athos ὠφελεῖς. The paragraph’s note identifies the bracketed connective but leaves these unbracketed conjectures indistinguishable from preserved witness wording.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the selected working readings, but extend the note to attribute these two conjectures and disclose the reported Athos alternatives. Identify the evidence as the supplied project apparatus transcription, not fresh manuscript verification. Any proposed English rendering of those alternatives requires separate review.

findings.source_quote: τοὺς δὲ λίθους, φησίν, οὓς εἶδες ἀποβεβλημένους, οὗτοι τὸ μὲν ὄνομα ἐφόρεσαν, τὸν δὲ ἱματισμὸν τῶν παρθένων οὐκ ἐνεδύσαντο.
findings.english_quote: “The stones you saw cast out,” he said, “are people who bore the name but did not put on the virgins’ clothing.”
findings.issue: The supplied apparatus identifies οὗτοι as Hilgenfeld’s conjecture, with αὐτοῖς reported for Athos. No note discloses this editorial reconstruction underlying the selected clause. The existing disclosures about other supplements do not cover it.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a source-choice note retaining οὗτοι in the working text while attributing the reported conjecture and preserving αὐτοῖς as the reported Athos alternative. Do not present an English alternative as established without reviewing its syntax.

findings.source_quote: καὶ ἄλλως ἄνθρωπος οὐ δύναται εὑρεθῆναι εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἐὰν μὴ αὗται αὐτὸν ἐνδύσωσι τὸ ἔνδυμα αὐτῶν· ἐὰν γὰρ τὸ ὄνομα μόνον λάβῃς, τὸ δὲ ἔνδυμα παρὰ τούτων μὴ λάβῃς, οὐδὲν ὠφελήσῃ
findings.english_quote: No one can be found in God’s kingdom unless they clothe that person in their garment. Receiving only the name will do you no good if you do not also receive their garment.
findings.issue: Although the necessary condition and negation are preserved, the note does not disclose the supplied apparatus’s identification of ἄλλως and ὠφελήσῃ as editorial conjectures, against reported Athos ἄλλος and ὠφελεῖς. Its disclosure of bracketed οὖν does not distinguish these additional reconstructed readings from preserved wording.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the working reading and add an attributed disclosure of both conjectures and the reported Athos alternatives. Any English alternatives should receive fresh review; no manuscript authentication should be claimed.

findings.source_quote: τοὺς δὲ λίθους, φησίν, οὓς εἶδες ἀποβεβλημένους, οὗτοι τὸ μὲν ὄνομα ἐφόρεσαν, τὸν δὲ ἱματισμὸν τῶν παρθένων οὐκ ἐνεδύσαντο.
findings.english_quote: The stones you saw cast out are people who bore the name but did not put on the virgins’ clothing.
findings.issue: The selected οὗτοι is reported in the supplied apparatus as Hilgenfeld’s conjecture against Athos αὐτοῖς, but the simplified edition supplies no disclosure of that reconstruction.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a note attributing the conjecture and disclosing the reported Athos wording while retaining the selected working text. Leave any unresolved alternative syntax explicitly unresolved rather than harmonizing it.

findings.source_quote: διὰ τοῦτο βλέπεις τὸν πύργον μονόλιθον γεγονότα [μετὰ] τῆς πέτρας. οὕτω καὶ οἱ πιστεύσαντες τῷ Κυρίῳ διὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐνδιδυσκόμενοι τὰ πνεύματα ταῦτα, ἔσονται εἰς ἓν πνεῦμα, καὶ ἓν σῶμα, μία χρόα τῶν ἱματίων αὐτῶν.
findings.english_quote: That is why the tower has become one stone with the rock.[c] Those who have believed in the Lord through his Son and put on these spirits will become one spirit and one body. Their garments will have one color.
findings.issue: The simplification omits βλέπεις, the statement that the interlocutor sees this result, and οὕτω καί, the explicit comparison connecting tower–rock unity with the believers’ unity. Merely placing the sentences together does not fully preserve that comparison.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “That is why you see that the tower has become one stone with the rock.[c] In the same way, those who have believed in the Lord through his Son and put on these spirits will become one spirit and one body. Their garments will have one color.”

findings.source_quote: Ἐπειδὴ πάντα σοι, φησί, μέλει, καὶ ἀκριβῶς ἐξετάζεις, ἄκουε περὶ τῶν ἀποβεβλημένων λίθων.
findings.english_quote: Everything concerns you, and you examine it closely. Listen to the explanation about the rejected stones.
findings.issue: The source explicitly makes the interlocutor’s concern and close examination the reason for the invitation to listen. Splitting the sentence removes the causal force of Ἐπειδή.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “Since everything concerns you and you examine it closely, listen to the explanation about the rejected stones.”

findings.source_quote: καὶ ἦν αὐτῶν ἓν πνεῦμα καὶ ἓν σῶμα [καὶ ἓν ἔνδυμα]· τὰ γὰρ αὐτὰ ἐφρόνουν καὶ δικαιοσύνην εἰργάζοντο.
findings.english_quote: They were with God’s servants and had one spirit, one body and one garment.[d] They thought the same things and practiced righteousness.
findings.issue: The independent second sentence omits γάρ’s explanatory connection: their shared thinking and practice of righteousness explain the preceding unity rather than merely adding another event or characteristic.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “They were with God’s servants and had one spirit, one body and one garment,[d] because they thought the same things and practiced righteousness.”

summary: Both editions preserve the passage’s difficult assertions, necessary conditions, negations, plural holy spirits, exchange of powers, and reader-facing “servants.” Their long-supplement notes accurately qualify the supplied comparison report and do not claim fresh manuscript verification. Both need fuller disclosure of reported unbracketed conjectures; the simplified edition also loses several explicit source relationships. These are bounded reviews against the selected working Greek and supplied reports, not certification of unseen manuscripts or exhaustive collation. Suggested replacements remain subject to fresh review.
